text:
oliver: quick heads-up — I repro'd a perf regression hitting upstream today on paged-attn when the allocator takes the reservation->fallback path. ~2x token latency for small batches (bs=1..4).

sasha: ugh. is that the same issue we saw with the hybrid slab before or a different hotspot?

oliver: different stack. seems linked to two things: (1) kernel chooser switching to fused FlashA-v2 for short sequences, (2) allocation fallback that walks the block table and inflates pagewalks. combined effect is a bunch of small GPU kernels + CPU-side page scans.

mike: can you paste the microbenchmark numbers?

oliver: here — running the small chat workload on a single A10G, model variant q4 and paged-kv enabled. timestamps are from perf-bot run.

```
config: batch_sizes=[1,2,4], seq_len=48, quant=q4, kernel_policy=auto, kv_paged=true
baseline (no fallback path):
  bs=1  p50=28ms  p95=34ms
  bs=2  p50=35ms  p95=44ms
  bs=4  p50=58ms  p95=72ms
with reservation->fallback path triggered:
  bs=1  p50=58ms  p95=95ms
  bs=2  p50=92ms  p95=130ms
  bs=4  p50=140ms p95=210ms
notes: kernel switch observed at runtime: fused-FA-v2 selected for seq<=64, but kernel launch overhead + small-kernel inefficiency kills us when per-request KV pagewalks spike.
```

raj: thanks, that matches a trace I pulled — CPU %busy goes up because the allocator does a per-shard block-table walk and then synchronously triggers device copies for spilled pages. we currently do a coarse lock around reservation.

sasha: is the fallback path doing per-request heap scans? we thought there was a short-circuit cache lookup.

oliver: the short-circuit exists but only for warm pages. cold pages hit the pagehouse, which does: lookup -> reserve slab -> if reserve fails -> fallback scan for fragmented slots -> coalesce or fall through to host staging. that scan is O(n) across slab entries for the shard. small batches amplify it.

mike: two immediate mitigations I can try: (A) bias kernel selection away from fused FA-v2 for seq<64 to reduce tiny-kernel overhead, (B) make the allocator prefer a transient staging buffer path earlier (avoid scan). which is lower risk?

sasha: (A) is low-risk and quick. kernel thresholds are config flags. (B) touches correctness of paging and may need more tests. but (B) probably gives bigger wins long-term.

perf-bot: benchmark/1823456789-run-1 finished. artifacts at s3://redwood-perf/1823456789/

oliver: I ran (A) locally — forcing kernel_policy=prefer-flash-v1 for seq<=64. microbench shows p50 for bs=1 down to 32ms (from 58ms) but bs=4 still higher than baseline. so kernel choice was ~30% of regression. remaining is allocator scan + device staging.

raj: attaching a short perf trace snippet (summarized):

```
CPU time breakdown:
  allocator: 42% (block_table_walk + coalesce)
  pagehouse lookup: 18%
  rpc: 5%
  GPU kernels: 35% (many tiny launches)

hot functions:
  BlockTable::scan_free_ranges
  PageHouse::stage_to_device_sync
  KernelChooser::choose_fused
```

ci-bot: @oliver created ticket #INF-1248 with attached perf traces and microbench results.

mike: ok plan: short-term = roll kernel bias back for short seqs + add an early fast-path in allocator to avoid the O(n) scan when total free < X. mid-term = async staging so page copies don't block the request thread and improve batching heuristics to coalesce tiny requests.

sasha: for async staging, we need to be careful about KV cache correctness and eviction order. also add instrumentation for 'reservation_fail_reason' to better metricize how often fallback hits.

oliver: agreed. I've added an exp flag kv.alloc.fast_fallback=true locally — it returns a transient staging slot when fragmentation > 60% instead of scanning. quick smoke shows bs=1 p50=36ms, bs=4 p50=68ms. not perfect but much closer.

raj: can we add a kernel-chooser metric output to the console so ops can see when fused vs flashv1 gets selected per-request? that will help correlate.

mike: yes, will add. also adding a batching heuristic tweak: if small-batch rate > 60% in 1s window, prefer non-fused kernels and increase dynamic micro-batching threshold to 8 tokens to reduce tiny-kernel churn.

oliver: I pushed the perf traces + minimal repro script to the ticket. If folks agree I'll open a PR with the kernel bias and the allocator fast_fallback flag behind feature gates.

sasha: please include a unit test for BlockTable::scan_free_ranges that simulates heavy fragmentation (many tiny frees) so we guard future regressions.

mike: I'll own the PR, add tests, and wire the console metrics. target: cut a canary tomorrow to verify on dedicated cluster.

oliver: thanks everyone. tagging @perf-bot to run the nightly battery after the canary. :thumbsup:

perf-bot: scheduled nightly-bench with tag canary-allocator-fix for 2026-03-18 03:00 UTC.
